The *Paṭhamanāgavimānavatthu* ("Elephant Mansion", Vv 60) is a verse text included in the *Vimānavatthu* of the Pali Tipiṭaka [SuttaCentral]. In this narrative, a celestial being (*deva*) describes the great karmic fruit earned by offering eight flowers at the stupa of the past Buddha Kassapa [SuttaCentral].

Textual reuse analyses conducted by DharmaNexus align the text with 31 other Pali works across 168 shared passages [DharmaNexus]. The extensive verse commentary preserved in the *Vimānavatthu-aṭṭhakathā* shares the highest degree of textual overlap (§0.4–3.4 closely matching §2691_6–2700) [DharmaNexus]. In addition, the text shares significant stock formulas and verse sequences with other stories within the *Vimānavatthu*, particularly another elephant-themed mansion story, the *Nāgavimānavatthu* (Vv 41, matching §1.3–3.4 with 0.98 similarity), as well as *Guttilavimānavatthu* (Vv 33) and *Paṭhamaagāriyavimānavatthu* (Vv 65) [DharmaNexus]. No significant cross-language alignments with Sanskrit, Chinese, or Tibetan corpora are identified by DharmaNexus [DharmaNexus]. SuttaCentral records four translations of the text in four modern languages [SuttaCentral].
